sentences.text:
This miscellaneous second appeal, under section 71(6) Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "the FSSA") has been filed against the order dated 5/3/2025 passed by IX District Judge,
Gwalior in RCA No. 6/2025, as well as, order dated 28/10/2024 passed by Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate, Gwalior in case No. Q/Food safety/12/2022.
2.

Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that complainant filed a complaint before the Adjudicating Officer alleging inter alia that on 23/10/2021, at about 11:35 a.m., FSO inspected the dairy where appellant was present and he informed that owner of dairy is his father Munnalal Sharma.
It was found that 30 kg of Paneer, 20 kg of curd, 12 kg of ghee and 35 liters of milk-mix were stored and were meant for sale.
Since the FSO had a suspicion that the aforesaid articles might be substandard, therefore samples were collected.

As per the report of the Food Analyst, the Paneer was found to be of substandard NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:30976 2 MSA-28-2025 quality.
Copy of report was sent to the appellant with an information that he can file an appeal under section 46(4) of FSSA and under 2.4.2(6) of Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011.
However, appellant did not prefer any appeal.
3. The Adjudicating Officer, after conducting the inquiry, held that appellant is guilty of violation of Ankit Sharma vs Nyaynirday Adhikari Khady Suraksha ...

sentences.text:
on 21 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98532034/
1 section 26 read with 51 of FSSA and, accordingly, imposed a penalty of rupees 1,50,000/-.

4. Being aggrieved by the said order, the appellant preferred an appeal which was registered as RCA No. 6/2025 and IX District Judge, Gwalior, by judgment dated 5/3/2025 dismissed the appeal after reducing the penalty amount from Rs.1,50,000/- to Rs.75,000/-.
5. A solitary ground has been raised by counsel for appellant that penalty amount may be further reduced.
6. Sale of substandard food articles is detrimental to the mankind.
The appellant could not point out any exceptional circumstance requiring further reduction in the penalty amount.
The appellate Authority has already shown sufficient leniency to the appellant while adjudicating the quantum of penalty.

Accordingly, this Court is of considered opinion that since 30 kg of Paneer which was stored by the appellant for sale was found to be of substandard quality, therefore no case is made out warranting interference.
7. Appeal fails and is, hereby, dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE (and)
